user_prompt: Meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials in adolescents and adults with asthma that is uncontrolled on medium-dose inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), comparing a medium-dose ICS combined with a long-acting beta2 agonist (LABA) in one inhaler against the same medium-dose ICS alone (for example fluticasone propionate/salmeterol vs fluticasone propionate, budesonide/formoterol vs budesonide, fluticasone furoate/vilanterol vs fluticasone furoate, beclomethasone/formoterol vs beclomethasone, mometasone/indacaterol vs mometasone).  Outcome: moderate to severe asthma exacerbations, as the number of participants with at least one moderate or severe exacerbation during the trial, out of the number randomised in each arm.  Effect measure: Risk Ratio (RR), ICS/LABA versus ICS alone, using participant counts. Values below 1 favour ICS/LABA.  Outcome rules: - Treatment arm = medium-dose ICS plus LABA. Control arm = the same medium-dose ICS alone, at the same dose. Ignore arms that are high-dose ICS, ICS plus LAMA, or any other comparator. - If a trial has several arms (for example a high-dose ICS arm or a high-dose ICS/LABA arm), use only the medium-dose ICS/LABA arm and the medium-dose ICS arm. If a control arm is shared with other comparisons, use its full reported size and events. - Count participants with at least one moderate or severe exacerbation (events needing systemic corticosteroids, an emergency visit or a hospital stay). If a trial reports only severe exacerbations or reports several definitions, use the definition closest to "moderate or severe". If it reports exacerbation rates only (events per person-year), use the participant counts if given in the text. - Use the full treatment period. - Use the number randomised or analysed as reported (intention-to-treat when available).  Include all randomised trials in the uploaded papers that fit this description. Do not exclude a trial because of its LABA or ICS brand, its dose schedule, its duration, or its size. Exclude only reviews, protocols and trials with no medium-dose ICS-alone control.
